req.title: Update form GET returns 200 for author
req.statement: The system shall serve the update form at GET /<id>/update when the current user is the post's author.
triggers: update form get returns 200 for author

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /<id>/update must return HTTP 200 when the current user is the post's author. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — authenticated author requests their own post's update form and receives 200; (2) negative — authenticated non-author requests another user's post update form and receives 403; (3) boundary — the lowest valid post id (id=1) is requested by its author (user 5/James) to verify the boundary of the id space. Additional mutation-resilient assertions check exact status codes (not ranges), exact redirect targets for unauthenticated access, and both sides of the author-check boolean.

tests.name: test_update_form_get_200_for_author
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in
Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
expected: Response body contains update form content
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_form_get_200_for_author():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'update' in r.data.lower() or b'Pillow delta willow' in r.data

test_update_form_get_200_for_author()
